main_body: A hexagonal coffin lid drawn flat and seen from above, with a gold cross on the lid. It tapers toward the foot. No front face is drawn below the lid.
top_band: none distinct: the whole body is a lid slab (orange-brown L~130-157) with a cross; no separate top band over a front face. A 1-row lighter band at rows 24 appears, but it is a lid trim, not a surface step.
evidence: The coffin is a top-down plan: a tapered hexagonal lid slab with a cross, outlined all round. The column scan shows no step from a light top band into a distinct front face. Rows 2-24 are the lid itself. Rows 25-29 are a darker foot area, about 5 rows, but this reads as a lid end and not a south face with its own details. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no recessed front. It matches the red top-down slab in the guide.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 10 colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 17-20 for the references and 38-40 distinct colours. Outline is dark brown (0% neutral), so it is tinted. Shading is limited to about 4 steps on the wood, plus a gold cross. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, with some variation on the lid. The piece is simple and clearly thinner than the references in colours and texture, so it is shallow next to them.
